issues.description: The abstract-lock invariant equates a held lock with a thread at cs, omitting the reachable unlock program-counter state in which the lock is still held.
issues.rationale: For one process, the allowed execution init -> start -> acquire_lock -> cs reaches pc[0]=unlock with locked=true: cs() changes the PC and stack but preserves locked; only the subsequent release_lock resets it. The set filtered by pc==cs is then empty, so both equivalences in not_locked_iff_no_cs are false. lemma_not_locked_iff_not_in_cs nevertheless promises this invariant always holds under init/next. The direct child repair counts both cs and unlock. This is a false abstract-state invariant, not a claim that executable mutual exclusion itself is broken. The file is introduced in this PR and absent from the archived comparison base.
